21.description: Saskatoon Police reported a second consecutive year of reduced missing persons reports, largely driven by fewer youth reports and effective collaboration with care homes and social services.

chips.text: Approved
4 for, 0 against
Commissioner Grier questioned if fewer reports meant better youth care or just reporting efficiency.
Youth under 18 comprise 69% of all missing person reports.
Police could not confirm if fewer reports meant improved youth connection to services.
Addictions, mental health, and poverty are key risk factors for missing persons.

23.description: Saskatoon Police Service updated its 2025 annual report and business plan, highlighting 36 initiatives. Key achievements include the Intimate Partner Violence Response Team and efforts against retail crime.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Commissioner Jeffries expressed pride in the Intimate Partner Violence Response Team.
Project Shield targeted retail businesses to address crime.
The Intimate Partner Violence Response Team supports victims of domestic violence.

24.description: Saskatoon Police Service will transfer $2,950,236 to its Capital Equipment and Technology Reserve and $1,070,690 to its Fiscal Stabilization Reserve from 2025 operating budget savings.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
$3M to the SPS Capital Equipment
$1.1M to the SPS Fiscal Stabilization Reserve
The fiscal stabilization fund was not depleted last year and is now bolstered.
Taxpayers benefit from efforts to keep future budget growth low.
Staff committed to detailed budget reviews for 2026-2029 pressures.

20.description: The Board decided not to submit a bid to host the Canadian Association of Police Governance's 2027 annual conference, citing significant resource pressure on the police service.

chips.text: Approved
5 for, 0 against
Commissioner Jeffries argued hosting in 2027 is not a smart move.
